document.title: Namespace capacity
document.description: CPU, memory and throttling per namespace. Assumes cAdvisor container_cpu_usage_seconds_total, container_memory_working_set_bytes, container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total, container_cpu_cfs_periods_total, container_network_receive_bytes_total and container_network_transmit_bytes_total, and kube-state-metrics kube_pod_info, kube_pod_container_resource_requests, kube_pod_container_resource_limits, kube_node_status_allocatable and kube_node_status_condition. Choose the namespace after importing.

widgets.title: CPU periods throttled
widgets.description: Share of CPU scheduling periods in which containers hit their limit. Sustained throttling means limits are below what the workload needs.

widgets.title: CPU use against requests
widgets.description: CPU use as a share of the CPU requested by each pod. A pod with no CPU request has no series here. Above 100% the pod uses more than it reserved.

widgets.title: Workload placement by node
widgets.query: label_replace(max by (node) (kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="cpu",unit="core"}) and on (node) count by (node) (kube_pod_info{namespace={{namespace}},node!=""}), "signal", "cpu-allocatable", "", "") or label_replace(max by (node) (kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="memory",unit="byte"}) and on (node) count by (node) (kube_pod_info{namespace={{namespace}},node!=""}), "signal", "memory-allocatable", "", "") or label_replace(sum by (pod, node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace={{namespace}},resource="cpu",unit="core"}), "signal", "cpu-request", "", "") or label_replace(sum by (pod, node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace={{namespace}},resource="memory",unit="byte"}), "signal", "memory-request", "", "") or label_replace(max by (node) (kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready",status="true"}) and on (node) count by (node) (kube_pod_info{namespace={{namespace}},node!=""}), "signal", "node-ready", "", "")

widgets.title: Requests and usage by pod
widgets.query: label_replace(sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace={{namespace}},container!="",container!="POD"}[5m])), "signal", "cpu-usage", "", "") or label_replace(sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace={{namespace}},container!="",container!="POD",resource="cpu",unit="core"}), "signal", "cpu-request", "", "") or label_replace(sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace={{namespace}},resource="cpu",unit="core"}), "signal", "cpu-limit", "", "") or label_replace(sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace={{namespace}},container!="",container!="POD"}), "signal", "memory-usage", "", "") or label_replace(sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace={{namespace}},container!="",container!="POD",resource="memory",unit="byte"}), "signal", "memory-request", "", "") or label_replace(sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace={{namespace}},resource="memory",unit="byte"}), "signal", "memory-limit", "", "")

document.title: Paprika control plane
document.description: Whether Paprika is keeping up: apps behind spec, exhausted retries, stuck releases, fleet index health, controller liveness, reconcile lag, phase counts, Insights query health, and container CPU and memory (container_cpu_usage_seconds_total, container_memory_working_set_bytes, kube_pod_container_resource_requests, kube_pod_container_resource_limits). Exhausted retries turn critical above zero; stale apps, stuck releases and a degraded fleet index turn warning.

widgets.title: Controller liveness
widgets.description: Seconds since the slowest controller last finished a reconcile successfully. Past five minutes the line enters the warning band.

widgets.title: Reconcile lag by application
widgets.description: The five applications furthest behind their latest spec, across namespaces. Zero means the application has reconciled.

widgets.title: Reconciles per second
widgets.description: Controller reconciliations per second, split by outcome. Error and fail outcomes appear beside success.

widgets.title: Applications by phase
widgets.description: Number of applications in each phase at each sample.

widgets.title: Releases by phase
widgets.description: Number of releases in each phase at each sample.

widgets.title: Stale applications over time
widgets.description: Applications behind their spec over the selected range. Shaded stretches mark a non-zero count.

widgets.title: Insights queries per second
widgets.description: Provider queries Insights runs per second, by provider, across all outcomes.

widgets.title: Insights query error ratio
widgets.description: Share of Insights provider queries that ended in an error. Above one percent the line enters the warning band.

widgets.title: Insights query p95 latency
widgets.description: 95th percentile duration of Insights provider queries over the last five minutes.

widgets.title: Insights capacity refusals per second
widgets.description: Queries refused with HTTP 429, split by pool. A gateway refusal names the limit that refused it: edge, budget, provider, queue, principal or unknown.

document.title: Service overview
document.description: The RED signals for one service: request rate, error ratio and latency. Assumes the common client-library metrics http_requests_total (with service, namespace and code labels, where code is the HTTP status) and http_request_duration_seconds_bucket (with service and namespace labels). The service variable defaults to .* (every service in the namespace); set it to one service name, or to a regex such as checkout|payments.

widgets.title: Error ratio over time
widgets.description: Share of requests answered with a 5xx status. Shading starts at 1% (warning) and 5% (critical).

widgets.title: Request latency
widgets.query: label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=~{{service}},namespace={{namespace}}}[5m]))), "quantile", "p50", "", "") or label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=~{{service}},namespace={{namespace}}}[5m]))), "quantile", "p95", "", "") or label_replace(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service=~{{service}},namespace={{namespace}}}[5m]))), "quantile", "p99", "", "")
widgets.description: Median, 95th and 99th percentile request duration, estimated from the latency histogram buckets.

document.title: SLO and burn rate
document.description: 99.9% availability objective over 30 days, as one SLO card with availability, error budget and multiwindow burn pairs. Its query is compiled from its config at run time. The burn-rate charts keep the 1-hour and 6-hour burn with the 2x, 6x and 14.4x bands. Assumes http_requests_total (service, namespace, code labels); 5xx is failure. Needs 30 days of counter retention. Auto refresh is 60s. Change the objective in the card's config.

widgets.title: Node resource inventory
widgets.query: {"sql":"SELECT n.node, round((h.cpu_ratio*100)::numeric,2)::double precision AS cpu, round((n.memory_ratio*100)::numeric,2)::double precision AS memory, round((n.disk_used_ratio*100)::numeric,2)::double precision AS disk, CASE WHEN n.disk_used_ratio > (1 - 40000000000.0 / 128000000000.0) THEN 'Disk pressure' WHEN h.cpu_ratio >= 0.7 THEN 'CPU near limit' ELSE 'Healthy' END AS status, (SELECT json_agg(json_build_object('timestamp',to_char(recent.observed_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC','YYYY-MM-DD\"T\"HH24:MI:SS\"Z\"'),'value',recent.cpu_ratio*100) ORDER BY recent.observed_at)::text FROM (SELECT x.observed_at,x.cpu_ratio FROM gallery.node_history x WHERE to_jsonb(x)->>'cluster'=to_jsonb(n)->>'cluster' AND x.node=n.node AND x.observed_at >= $2::timestamptz AND x.observed_at <= $3::timestamptz ORDER BY x.observed_at DESC LIMIT 240) recent) AS history FROM gallery.nodes n JOIN LATERAL (SELECT cpu_ratio FROM gallery.node_history x WHERE to_jsonb(x)->>'cluster'=to_jsonb(n)->>'cluster' AND x.node=n.node AND x.observed_at >= $2::timestamptz AND x.observed_at <= $3::timestamptz ORDER BY observed_at DESC LIMIT 1) h ON true WHERE to_jsonb(n)->>'cluster'=$1 ORDER BY cpu DESC","parameters":[{{cluster}},{"range":"start"},{"range":"end"}]}
widgets.description: CPU uses the latest observation in the selected range and the sparkline shows up to its latest 240 samples. Memory and disk are seed-time snapshots.

widgets.title: Selected node · resources
widgets.query: {"sql":"SELECT node, namespace, cores, round((memory_ratio*100)::numeric,1)::double precision AS memory_percent, round((disk_used_ratio*100)::numeric,1)::double precision AS disk_percent FROM gallery.nodes n WHERE to_jsonb(n)->>'cluster'=$1 AND node=$2","parameters":[{{cluster}},{{node}}]}

document.title: Market Lens · Local demo
document.description: Synthetic local provider data. Sector filters the summary and company table; composition and sector trends show all sectors. Company details, ranks and composition are seed-time snapshots; history charts and sparklines use the selected time range. Composition shows the four largest companies per sector.

widgets.title: Company composition by market cap
widgets.query: {"sql":"SELECT c.symbol AS ticker, c.name AS company, c.sector, (c.market_cap/1000000000.0)::double precision AS market_cap, c.short_percent AS short_interest FROM gallery.companies c WHERE c.symbol IN (SELECT x.symbol FROM gallery.companies x WHERE x.sector=c.sector ORDER BY x.market_cap DESC LIMIT 4) ORDER BY c.sector, c.market_cap DESC","parameters":[]}

widgets.title: Company short positions
widgets.query: {"sql":"SELECT c.symbol AS ticker,c.name AS company,c.sector,(c.market_cap/1000000000.0)::double precision AS market_cap,c.short_percent AS short_interest,(SELECT json_agg(json_build_object('timestamp',to_char(recent.observed_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC','YYYY-MM-DD\"T\"HH24:MI:SS\"Z\"'),'value',recent.value) ORDER BY recent.observed_at)::text FROM (SELECT h.observed_at,h.value FROM gallery.company_history h WHERE h.symbol=c.symbol AND h.observed_at >= $2::timestamptz AND h.observed_at <= $3::timestamptz ORDER BY h.observed_at DESC LIMIT 240) recent) AS history FROM gallery.companies c WHERE c.sector=$1 ORDER BY c.short_percent DESC","parameters":[{{sector}},{"range":"start"},{"range":"end"}]}

widgets.title: Short interest by sector · recent history
widgets.query: {"sql":"SELECT h.observed_at AS day, c.sector, avg(h.value)::double precision AS short_interest FROM gallery.company_history h JOIN gallery.companies c ON c.symbol=h.symbol WHERE h.observed_at >= $1::timestamptz AND h.observed_at <= $2::timestamptz GROUP BY h.observed_at,c.sector ORDER BY h.observed_at,c.sector","parameters":[{"range":"start"},{"range":"end"}]}

widgets.query: {"sql":"SELECT h.observed_at AS day,avg(h.value)::double precision AS short_interest,avg(c.coverage_percent)::double precision AS coverage FROM gallery.company_history h JOIN gallery.companies c ON c.symbol=h.symbol WHERE c.sector=$1 AND h.observed_at >= $2::timestamptz AND h.observed_at <= $3::timestamptz GROUP BY h.observed_at ORDER BY h.observed_at","parameters":[{{sector}},{"range":"start"},{"range":"end"}]}

document.title: Reliability Room · Local demo
document.description: Synthetic sample data from the local Prometheus, Tempo and PostgreSQL providers. The SLO card, the services card and the burn rates all describe synthetic request errors against a 99.9% objective over 30 days. Budget remaining can be negative once the objective is overspent.

widgets.title: Incident severity by day · UTC
widgets.query: {"sql":"SELECT started_at AS date, summary AS label, severity AS status, CASE severity WHEN 'warning' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'critical' THEN 2.0 ELSE NULL END::double precision AS value FROM gallery.incidents i WHERE service=$1 AND to_jsonb(i)->>'cluster'='omega' AND started_at>=$2::timestamptz AND started_at<=$3::timestamptz UNION ALL SELECT started_at AS date, summary AS label, severity AS status, NULL::double precision AS value FROM gallery.incident_severity_samples s WHERE service=$1 AND to_jsonb(s)->>'cluster'='omega' AND started_at>=$2::timestamptz AND started_at<=$3::timestamptz ORDER BY date DESC","parameters":[{{service}},{"range":"start"},{"range":"end"}]}

widgets.title: Recent incidents
widgets.query: {"sql":"SELECT started_at AS date,service,summary AS label,(extract(epoch FROM (least(coalesce(ended_at,$3::timestamptz),$3::timestamptz)-started_at))/60.0)::double precision AS value,severity AS status,CASE WHEN ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at>$3::timestamptz THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Resolved' END AS state FROM gallery.incidents i WHERE service=$1 AND to_jsonb(i)->>'cluster'='omega' AND started_at<=$3::timestamptz AND (ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at>=$2::timestamptz) ORDER BY started_at DESC","parameters":[{{service}},{"range":"start"},{"range":"end"}]}

document.title: Paprika control plane · Local demo
document.description: Whether Paprika is keeping up: apps behind spec, exhausted retries, stuck releases, fleet index health, controller liveness, reconcile lag, phase counts, Insights query health, and container CPU and memory (container_cpu_usage_seconds_total, container_memory_working_set_bytes, kube_pod_container_resource_requests, kube_pod_container_resource_limits). Exhausted retries turn critical above zero; stale apps, stuck releases and a degraded fleet index turn warning.

widgets.title: Controller liveness
widgets.description: Seconds since the slowest controller last finished a reconcile successfully. Past five minutes the line enters the warning band.

widgets.title: Reconcile lag by application
widgets.description: The five applications furthest behind their latest spec, across namespaces. Zero means the application has reconciled.

widgets.title: Reconciles per second
widgets.description: Controller reconciliations per second, split by outcome. Error and fail outcomes appear beside success.

widgets.title: Applications by phase
widgets.description: Number of applications in each phase at each sample.

widgets.title: Releases by phase
widgets.description: Number of releases in each phase at each sample.

widgets.title: Stale applications over time
widgets.description: Applications behind their spec over the selected range. Shaded stretches mark a non-zero count.

widgets.title: Insights queries per second
widgets.description: Provider queries Insights runs per second, by provider, across all outcomes.

widgets.title: Insights query error ratio
widgets.description: Share of Insights provider queries that ended in an error. Above one percent the line enters the warning band.

widgets.title: Insights query p95 latency
widgets.description: 95th percentile duration of Insights provider queries over the last five minutes.

widgets.title: Insights capacity refusals per second
widgets.description: Queries refused with HTTP 429, split by pool. A gateway refusal names the limit that refused it: edge, budget, provider, queue, principal or unknown.
